resale_co.name: CCO (Continued Certificate of Occupancy) for resale
resale_co.issued_by: Upper Freehold Township Housing Inspector (application to the Construction Office)
requirements: Onsite inspection by the Housing Inspector for compliance with the Housing Code and applicable safety codes
Visual inspection of the septic system (if any), scheduled with the Freehold Area Health Department
Well water test by a State certified laboratory (if the home has a well), with results sent to the Freehold Area Health Department
Certificate of Compliance from the Freehold Area Health Department before the CCO is issued
Fee paid by cash or check only, payable to Upper Freehold Township

fees.label: CCO inspection for resale or rental
fees.quote: A $100.00 fee is required paid by cash or check only (checks made payable to Upper Freehold Township).

fees.label: Resale or rental Certificate of Occupancy inspection fee (Township Code 11-3.7)
fees.quote: An applicant is required to submit an application for the re-sale or rental of residential property along with a $100 inspection fee to the Construction Office of the Township.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Submit the Township's Resale or Rental Application with the $100 fee (cash or check payable to Upper Freehold Township) to the Construction Office / Housing Department, 314 Route 539, Cream Ridge, NJ 08514. An appointment is then scheduled with the Housing Inspector. If the home has a septic system or well, call the Freehold Area Health Department for the septic inspection and send it the well water test results. Office hours are Monday to Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:15 p.m.

evidence.quote: A CCO (Continued Certificate of Occupancy) is required any time occupancy changes for all Resale & Rental Properties.
An onsite inspection will be conducted to assess compliance with applicable safety codes.
A Certificate of Occupancy is required for the resale or rental of residential property previously issued a Certificate of Occupancy upon initial occupation of the residence.
An appointment is scheduled with the Housing Inspector.
Upon approval of the septic system inspection and well water results, the Freehold Area Health Department will issue a Certificate of Compliance.

resale_co.notes: The Housing Department page and Township Code 11-3.7 (read through the ecode360 print view) agree on the $100 fee. The page links a "2022 RESALE OR RENTAL APPLICATION" PDF through a document-download widget; the file opens but its text could not be extracted (likely a scan), so its contents were not checked. The site sits behind a bot check and may block automated fetches. Hailey Dries, 609-758-7738 Ext. 212, Hdries@uftnj.com, is also listed on the Housing Department page (no title shown).

requirements: Certificate of smoke detector and carbon monoxide detector compliance required under N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3 before a 1 or 2 family home changes occupants

No Township checklist was found online; state rules apply (smoke alarm on each level and outside sleeping areas, 10-year sealed battery units where battery-only, CO alarm near sleeping areas when there is a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage)

authorities.name: Upper Freehold Township (Bureau of Fire Prevention / Construction office)
authorities.area_served: Entire township (the Township is also the LEA for Allentown Borough)
authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on business days between the application and the occupant change: more than 10 business days for the lowest fee.

fees.label: Smoke and CO certificate, application received more than 10 business days before occupant change
Application received 4 to 10 business days before occupant change
Application received less than 4 business days before occupant change
fees.quote: Less than 4 business days before occupant change: $161

authorities.how_to_apply: No online application was found. Call the Township at 609-758-7738 or the Fire Official at 609-259-7665 to request the smoke and CO certificate inspection.

fire_cert.notes: Township Code 14-5 (Fire Prevention, amended by Ord. No. 294-18, read through the ecode360 page) sets the $45 / $90 / $161 fees; the first tier text reads "When the application is received more than 10 business days before occupant change: $45". The NJ DCA fire directory lists the smoke detector compliance office as the Upper Freehold Construction office at 314 Route 539 (phone (609) 758-7738), while the Fire Official is Alex Nebbia (609) 259-7665. Which office actually schedules the sale inspection was not stated online.

other_items.label: Septic inspection and well water test (Freehold Area Health Department)
other_items.detail: For homes with a septic system, a visual septic inspection by the Freehold Area Health Department is required; homes on a well need a well water test by a State certified lab. The Health Department then issues a Certificate of Compliance, which the Housing Inspector needs before issuing the CCO.
